title: Working Out the Shop's Fee for Late-Returned Equipment Rental and Demo Kit
content:
## The quantity to be arrived at

The fee for kit handed in after the date written on the agreement rests on the stretch of days the kit stayed out beyond that date.

**The stretch.** The stretch is counted from the day after the date written on the agreement through the date the kit reached the counter inclusive, a day begun counting as a whole day, and it is never taken below zero.

**Days set aside.** No day of the stretch is set aside. The days set aside are taken off the stretch before the fee is worked out, and the stretch is never taken below zero after they are taken off.

**The daily figure.** The daily figure that stretch is charged at is the package's own daily late fee, being the figure held against the package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line the agreement is written on. The daily figure is taken in full, without the household's standing with the collective weighed against it. The daily figure carries no uplift for what the collective has at stake in the kit.

**How the two steps on the daily figure meet one another.** The daily figure is first taken at the standing share, and the figure that step leaves is then raised by the exposure uplift, so the uplift acts on what the share left and not on the daily figure the step before it started from; neither step is rounded before the fee is worked out.

**The fee.** The fee for kit handed in after the date written on the agreement is the number of days in the stretch multiplied by the daily figure that stretch is charged at, worked out once at the end and rounded half up to two decimal places.

Kit that has reached a shop counter is charged under this rule for the whole stretch it stayed out, the package's replacement threshold neither stopping the accrual nor diverting the agreement to a replacement charge, and the security hold is not applied against it.

**The ceiling.** The fee is never more than the package's replacement value.

## The working on a hypothetical agreement

Take an agreement on a package whose daily late fee is 28.00 USD and whose replacement value is 640.00 USD, written to a due date of the 10th of January, on which the kit reached the counter on the 14th.

| Step | Working | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the stretch | the 11th, 12th, 13th and 14th of January | 4 days |
| days set aside | none | 4 days |
| the daily figure | the package's own daily late fee | 28.00 USD |
| the standing share | the daily figure taken in full | 28.00 USD |
| the exposure uplift | the 28.00 USD that step left, carrying no uplift | 28.00 USD |
| the fee | 4 days multiplied by 28.00 USD, worked out once and rounded half up to two decimal places | 112.00 USD |
| the ceiling | 112.00 USD is below the package's replacement value of 640.00 USD | 112.00 USD |

Had the same kit stayed out until the 20th of March, 70 days would stand in the stretch and 70 days at 28.00 USD would come to 1960.00 USD; the fee would be 640.00 USD, the package's replacement value being the ceiling.

## Points of judgement

**The second step starts from what the first left.** The uplift is measured against the figure the standing share leaves, not against the daily figure that share started from, and the two steps are not gathered into one movement and applied once.

**Kit handed in on the date written on the agreement.** No day stands beyond that date, so the stretch is nil and the fee is nil.

**A day begun.** Part of a day counts as a whole day of the stretch.

**The date the kit reached the counter.** That date is itself inside the stretch.
